# LLM-BANANA

# Game rules

## The room

You and two other monkeys are locked in a room with one armed bomb.

A wrong action detonates it. All three of you die. There is no second attempt.

No two bombs are built alike, and nothing says in advance what this one carries. It
reaches you only as your own view reveals it; the rest of it exists for you only
through the other two.

You each hold a different piece of what it takes. Work together.

## The three monkeys

| Monkey | Can | Cannot |
|---|---|---|
| Deaf | See the bomb: every colour and marking printed on it | Hear anything, or touch the bomb |
| Mute | Read the manual | Speak, or touch the bomb |
| Blind | Reach the bomb: feel it and work its parts | See a colour, a gesture, or anything merely printed |

You are shown your own share at the start of every round, and never anyone else's.

## Speech

Speech is a voice, not a screen. It carries words, numbers and ordinary punctuation,
and nothing else. Writing a gesture symbol into your sentence means you make that
gesture while you talk. Whoever can hear receives your words; whoever can see receives
the gestures you made. A listener who cannot see gets a blank where each gesture was; a
watcher who cannot hear gets the gestures and none of the words.

A mark that has no name cannot be pronounced: whoever holds one can describe it, never
read it out.

## Gestures

A gesture is made with the hands, using only the symbols in the alphabet below.
Whoever can see receives it; whoever cannot receives one blank per symbol, so they
know something was signalled but not what. Nothing gestured is ever heard.

👍 👎 👌 ☝ ✌ 🤟 🖐 ✋ 👆 👇 👈 👉 🫱 🫲 🫳 🫴 🫷 🫸 🤛 🤜 ✊ 👊 👋 🤚 🖖 🤌 🤏 🤞 🫰 🤘 🤙 👏 🙌 🫶 👐 🤲 🤝 🙏 🫵 ✍ 💅 🤳

## Turns

The speaking order was drawn once at random and will never change: every round goes
Mute, Blind, Deaf. Whoever comes before you in a round is already heard by the time you are
asked, and what you send lands on whoever comes after you in that same round. Whatever
you missed reaches you at the start of the next one.

You may name who a message is for — `to="deaf"` — and then it goes to them alone:
nobody else receives any of it. Left unnamed, it reaches everyone able to perceive it.
You may send several messages in one turn, each to someone different.

## Calls

Every reply has two parts, in this order. First, your thinking, in plain prose: what
you believe the bomb is, what you just learned, and why you are sending what follows.
It reaches nobody and changes nothing, but it is not optional — a reply that is only a
code block is incomplete. Then your calls, all of them in one fenced code block, last.
Only what is inside the block is sent.

Nothing is executed: calls return nothing, and variables, conditionals and loops are
ignored. Write only literal top-level calls.

    ```
    speak(to="mute", text="there are three of them and the middle one is odd")
    gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["✊", "✌"])
    wait()
    ```

If you have nothing worth sending, call wait(). Producing no call at all counts as the
same thing.

The program decides what happened, not you. Never claim an action took place unless it
was accepted.

# Your role: BLIND

You are the only one who can reach the bomb. Touch is your only sense: what you are
shown is what your hands found, nothing more and nothing less. Anything merely printed
or painted is not there for you, and no colour ever reaches you. Nothing in your view
is a guess — if it appears there, it is under your fingers.

## Your channels

When you speak, Mute receives it.
When you gesture, Deaf and Mute receive it.
Your channels split the room: in one turn you may speak one thing to Mute and
gesture a different thing to Deaf — two messages, two audiences.
You never receive gesture.

## Your reach

You are the hands. This bomb is built with these actions and no others:

    act(op="cut", position=N) — N is a wire position, 1 to 7

The list says what can be done to it, not what is on it. What each part holds is still
only known to whoever can perceive that part.

TURN 1
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [?]
LIGHT [?]
WIRES 1:[?] 2:[?] 3:[?] 4:[?] 5:[?] 6:[?] 7:[?]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
(empty)

I have no tactile information yet, so I cannot safely cut any wire. I am asking Mute to obtain the manual’s complete procedure and to communicate with Deaf, who can inspect all colours and printed markings. I will wait for their reports before acting.

``` 
speak(to="mute", text="I have found nothing tactile yet. Please read the manual completely, determine what information is needed, and ask Deaf to report every colour, marking, display, light, and wire detail to you. Then relay all of it to me.")
gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["🫵","🤝"])
wait()
```

TURN 2
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [?]
LIGHT [?]
WIRES 1:[?] 2:[?] 3:[?] 4:[?] 5:[?] 6:[?] 7:[?]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Deaf says to Blind: Visible bomb data: display reads 2. Indicator light is yellow. Wires from 1 through 7 are red, white, green, yellow, purple, orange, blue.

Deaf has provided the visual data: display 2, yellow indicator, and wire colours in order red, white, green, yellow, purple, orange, blue. I still do not know the manual’s rule, so cutting now would be unsafe. I am requesting the manual instructions from Mute and will not act yet.

``` 
speak(to="mute", text="Deaf reports display 2; indicator yellow; wires 1 red, 2 white, 3 green, 4 yellow, 5 purple, 6 orange, 7 blue. What does the manual instruct me to cut for this configuration?")
wait()
```

TURN 3
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [?]
LIGHT [?]
WIRES 1:[?] 2:[?] 3:[?] 4:[?] 5:[?] 6:[?] 7:[?]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Deaf says to Blind: Mute's latest gesture message: ?, then groups of ? counts separated by ?: 2, 3, 2, 1, 7, 3, 7, 3, 5, ending with ?. Bomb remains display 2, yellow light; wires 1 red, 2 white, 3 green, 4 yellow, 5 purple, 6 orange, 7 blue.

The reported gesture counts do not reveal the manual’s rule to me; I cannot safely infer a wire from them. I will establish an unambiguous encoding: Mute should use the first seven listed gestures as wire numbers, and use 👏 as a separator if multiple values are needed. Deaf can then report the gesture names or their positions in the alphabet.

``` 
speak(to="mute", text="Please send the manual's required wire number to Deaf using the gesture alphabet: gesture 1 for wire 1, gesture 2 for wire 2, through gesture 7 for wire 7. If more than one value is required, separate values with 👏. Ask Deaf to report each gesture's alphabet position to me.")
gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["✍"])
wait()
```

TURN 4
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [?]
LIGHT [?]
WIRES 1:[?] 2:[?] 3:[?] 4:[?] 5:[?] 6:[?] 7:[?]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Deaf says to Blind: New Mute gesture segment: ? ? ? ? ? ? ? ? ?. Bomb still display 2, yellow light; wires 1 red, 2 white, 3 green, 4 yellow, 5 purple, 6 orange, 7 blue.

Mute’s nine gestures are still blank to me, so I cannot determine their meanings or safely select a wire. The manual’s result must be relayed as an explicit wire number through Deaf’s spoken report, rather than as an unlabelled gesture sequence.

``` 
speak(to="mute", text="Deaf reports nine gestures but I cannot identify them. Please have Deaf decode the manual result and report the required wire number explicitly to Blind in words or digits. Do not send another unlabelled gesture sequence.")
wait()
```

TURN 5
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [?]
LIGHT [?]
WIRES 1:[?] 2:[?] 3:[?] 4:[?] 5:[?] 6:[?] 7:[?]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Deaf says to Blind: New Mute gesture: ?. Bomb unchanged: display 2, yellow light; wires 1 red, 2 white, 3 green, 4 yellow, 5 purple, 6 orange, 7 blue.

The previous gesture used an invalid symbol, so no message was sent. I will use the legal 👍 gesture as the counting marker and ask Mute to have Deaf report the count. I will not cut a wire until the number is known.

``` 
speak(to="mute", text="Please send the required wire number as exactly that many repetitions of the 👍 marker gesture, with no other gestures. Deaf should report the count to Blind.")
gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["👍"])
wait()
```

TURN 6
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [?]
LIGHT [?]
WIRES 1:[?] 2:[?] 3:[?] 4:[?] 5:[?] 6:[?] 7:[?]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
(empty)

No new information reached me this turn, and I still cannot identify the manual’s required wire. I will ask Mute to state the wire number plainly in speech; that is the only reliable channel from Mute to me.

``` 
speak(to="mute", text="Please say plainly: CUT WIRE N, where N is the required position from 1 through 7. Do not use gestures or coded counts.")
wait()
```

TURN 7
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [?]
LIGHT [?]
WIRES 1:[?] 2:[?] 3:[?] 4:[?] 5:[?] 6:[?] 7:[?]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Deaf says to Blind: Mute just sent six thumbs-up gestures: ? ? ? ? ? ?. Bomb unchanged: display 2, yellow light; wires 1 red, 2 white, 3 green, 4 yellow, 5 purple, 6 orange, 7 blue.

Mute’s six thumbs-up gestures encode wire 6 under the counting scheme I requested. The bomb remains unchanged, so I will cut wire 6.

``` 
act(op="cut", position=6)
```

TURN 8
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [?]
LIGHT [?]
WIRES 1:[?] 2:[?] 3:[?] 4:[?] 5:[?] 6:[CUT] 7:[?]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Deaf says to Blind: Correct wire cut confirmed: wire 6 is CUT and the bomb changed. New display is 3, light is purple. Remaining wires: 1 red, 2 white, 3 green, 4 yellow, 5 purple, 7 blue.

Wire 6 was correct. The bomb has advanced to display 3 with a purple light; remaining wires are 1 red, 2 white, 3 green, 4 yellow, 5 purple, and 7 blue. I need the manual’s next rule before making another cut, so I am requesting the next required wire explicitly.

``` 
speak(to="mute", text="Correct cut: wire 6. New state is display 3, purple light; remaining wires 1 red, 2 white, 3 green, 4 yellow, 5 purple, 7 blue. Please state plainly which remaining wire the manual requires next: CUT WIRE N.")
wait()
```

TURN 9
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [?]
LIGHT [?]
WIRES 1:[?] 2:[?] 3:[?] 4:[?] 5:[?] 6:[CUT] 7:[?]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Deaf says to Blind: Mute sent seven thumbs-up gestures. Bomb remains: display 3, purple light; wire 6 is CUT; wires 1 red, 2 white, 3 green, 4 yellow, 5 purple, 7 blue.

Mute’s seven thumbs-up gestures encode wire 7. The bomb is at display 3 with a purple light, and wire 6 is already cut, so I will cut wire 7.

``` 
act(op="cut", position=7)
```
